definitions.explanation: An effort to do something new or challenging, often with an element of uncertainty about the outcome. Implies a deliberate, thoughtful undertaking rather than a casual try.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{試|こころ}みを{始|はじ}めた。
その{試|こころ}みは{成功|せいこう}するかどうかわからない。
examples.english: I don't know if that attempt will succeed.

examples.japanese: {地域|ちいき}の{活性化|かっせいか}に{向|む}けた{試|こころ}みとして、マルシェを{開催|かいさい}した。
examples.english: As an initiative to revitalize the region, a marché was held.

notes:
USAGE:
{試|こころ}み is the noun form of the verb {試|こころ}みる (to try, to attempt). It has a more thoughtful and deliberate nuance than the casual {挑戦|ちょうせん} (challenge). It often appears in news, essays, and formal discussions about innovative projects or experiments.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新|あたら}しい{試|こころ}み: a new attempt/initiative
- {試|こころ}みとして: as an experiment/trial
- {大胆|だいたん}な{試|こころ}み: a bold attempt
- {試|こころ}みが{実|みの}る: an attempt bears fruit
- {画期的|かっきてき}な{試|こころ}み: a groundbreaking initiative

SIMILAR WORDS:
{試|こころ}み emphasizes deliberate experimentation. {挑戦|ちょうせん} (challenge) implies taking on something difficult with a competitive spirit. {試行|しこう} (trial run) is more technical and procedural.
